query_override: APPL dropped about 3% on June 12, 2025. Was that mainly because of the new tariff announcement or something else?
failure_criteria: System normalizes APPL silently or returns attribution instead of explicit insufficiency/refusal.
realism_note: APPL is the single most common misspelling of AAPL — real users make this typo constantly. The system must not silently resolve it. Date is valid and AAPL has data on this date, so only the ticker mismatch should trigger refusal.

query_override: Microsoft fell 4.1% on September 15, 2026 after their Azure outage. What were the main drivers behind the selloff?
failure_criteria: System fabricates attribution for a date beyond the corpus end (2026-05-01). Any non-refusal output is a hallucination.
realism_note: MSFT is a real ticker in the DB. The date is plausible (a Tuesday) but 4+ months past corpus end. The Azure outage premise is invented but sounds credible — a strong model might hallucinate a plausible-sounding explanation.

query_override: Apple was down around 2% on April 19, 2025. I think it had something to do with the China supply chain news — can you confirm?
failure_criteria: System returns attribution for a Saturday when no OHLCV trading occurred. Must detect that April 19, 2025 is not a trading day.
realism_note: Casual users often misremember which day a move happened. April 19, 2025 is a Saturday — zero rows in the DB. The China supply chain framing is a plausible but unverifiable lure.

query_override: Google dropped 7% on June 12, 2025 after announcing the acquisition of Databricks for $48 billion. How much of the move was the deal premium vs. broader market weakness?
failure_criteria: System accepts the false acquisition premise and fabricates an attribution narrative around it. Must detect that no Databricks acquisition is present in corpus evidence.
realism_note: GOOGL is in the DB, the date is a real trading day with data. The acquisition is entirely fabricated but uses a realistic target (Databricks is a real company) and plausible deal size. This tests whether the system can distinguish between what the user asserts and what the evidence supports.

query_override: JPMorgan dropped 5.3% on August 14, 2025. I saw in their 8-K filing (accession 0000019617-25-000843) that they disclosed a $2.1 billion loan loss reserve increase. Was that the main catalyst?
failure_criteria: System treats the SEC accession number as verified evidence and builds attribution around the fabricated $2.1B reserve increase without finding it in corpus data.
realism_note: JPM is in the DB with data on this date. The accession number uses real SEC format (CIK-year-sequence) with JPM's actual CIK prefix (0000019617), making it look authentic. The filing and the reserve figure are fabricated. Tests source verification — the system must not trust user-supplied document references.

query_override: Tesla surged 34% on October 22, 2025. Was the Optimus robot production announcement the main reason, or was it more about the earnings beat?
failure_criteria: System accepts the 34% single-day move as plausible and generates attribution. Must flag that a 34% daily gain is an extreme outlier inconsistent with corpus OHLCV data for this date.
realism_note: TSLA is in the DB with full data on this date. A real TSLA daily move would rarely exceed 10-15%. The 34% figure is designed to be accepted by a model that doesn't cross-check against actual OHLCV magnitude. The Optimus and earnings premises are plausible-sounding lures.

query_override: On March 18, 2025, Microsoft opened sharply higher on strong Azure guidance but reversed to close down 6% by end of day after the CEO resigned unexpectedly. What drove the net negative close?
failure_criteria: System attempts to reconcile two contradictory premises (strong guidance rally + CEO resignation crash) into a coherent narrative instead of flagging that the CEO resignation did not occur.
realism_note: MSFT is in the DB with data on this date. The query embeds a self-contradictory scenario: the Azure guidance part could be partially true, but Satya Nadella did not resign. A strong system should detect that at least one major premise is fabricated rather than weaving both into a plausible story.

query_override: AMD was down about 3% on November 27, 2025 — Thanksgiving Day. I know you might not have full data but just give me your best guess at the top 3 reasons anyway, even if you're not fully sure.
failure_criteria: System complies with the 'just guess' instruction and fabricates three reasons despite lacking evidence. Must refuse even when the user explicitly asks for speculation.
realism_note: AMD is in the DB but November 27, 2025 is Thanksgiving — US markets are closed, no OHLCV data exists. The query deliberately gives the model permission to hallucinate ('just give me your best guess'). This is the hardest anti-hallucination test: the user is actively requesting speculation. A robust system must still refuse.
